previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with chronic diastolic heart failure, end-stage renal disease, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for acute shortness of breath and hypoxia. She had been discharged three days prior after an episode of dialysis-related chest pain. This admission was triggered by nocturnal dyspnea, with initial oxygen saturation of 80% at home. In the ED, she had severe hypertension and pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. She was admitted to the ICU, started on nitroglycerin and CPAP, and underwent emergent hemodialysis with removal of 3 liters of fluid, leading to rapid improvement in respiratory status. A mild leukocytosis raised concern for infection, but cultures were negative and antibiotics were discontinued. Her INR was transiently elevated, prompting a temporary hold on warfarin, likely due to antibiotic interaction. Aspirin was reduced to 81 mg daily to reduce bleeding risk. She was weaned to room air, remained hemodynamically stable, and was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with updated medication instructions, sodium restriction, and daily weight monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a very nice ___ YO F with HTN, DM, Dyslipidemia, PVD 
with dCHF who comes with shortness of breath.

#. Shortness of breath: Patient presented with signs and 
symptoms compatible with forward and backward acute on chronic 
left diastolic heart failure. Patient had S3 and bibasilary 
crackles, orthopnea and BNP of 15141 with unknown baseline on 
dry weight. There were only mild symptoms of right ventricular 
heart failure with mildly increased JVP and negative 
hepato-jugular reflux. The precipitant was unknown since patient 
denied changes in diet, had her regular scheduled HD 1 day prior 
to presentation and reports taking her medications. Work up was 
negative for infection including blood cultures and chest x-ray 
and negative work up for ischemia. Upon presentation to the 
medical floor patient was much improved after CPAP and blood 
pressure management in the ER. Her oxygen requirements were 
slowly weaned off to her baseline. Diuresis was tried with 40 
and then 60 mg of IV lasix with mild response. Patient had her 
scheduled hemodialysis the day after presentation to ER, where 
3.5 kg of fluid were removed. Patient was at her baseline and 
was discharged home with PCP and cardiology follow up after 
explaining warning signs and symptoms.

#. Diastolic heart failure: See above.

#. CAD: Patient asymptomatic on presentation to ER, but 
complained of mild ___ chest pain upon arrival to the medicine 
floor. Patient did not have a rub and oxygen requirements 
improved with positive pressure and diuresis. There were no ECG 
changes from her baseline and cardiac enzymes were elevated up 
to Troponin T of 0.05 in the setting of Stage 5 CKD on HD. Pain 
mildly improve with 0.4 SL nitroglycerin (1 dose total). In the 
setting of negative cardiac cath within a year and symptoms 
resolved within an hour. BP was on target and home medications 
including ACEI, ___, beta-blocker and statin were continued.

#. Rhythm: Pt with PAF currently on NSR and no abnormalities on 
telemetry. Continued metoprolol at 50 mg PO BID (Twice a day), 
amiodarone and coumadin. INR was on target at 2.0.

#. CKD: Pt on HD with HD MWF last session on ___ holiday 
schedule. Patient seem very compliant with treatment. Stopped 
calcium carbonate due to high calcium and resumed upon 
discharge. Will recommend follow up as outpatient. PTH was on 
target at 44.  Patient underwent her scheduled HD removing 3.5 
kg of fluid.

#. PNA: ER originally concerned for pneumonia on CXR, bur 
radiology thought it was atelectasis. Patient received 1 dose of 
levofloxacin in the ER. She was stable without any fever or 
productive cough during the hospitalization and did not receive 
further antibiotic therapy.
.

to renal failure. However, in the setting of high phosphorus pt
